- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid mean reversion trap.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in second half of horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not exceed 1.5% above prior high; cap at 1.5% above recent 5-day average.
